title: Midnight triage rundown — 2027-01-05
body:
Summary:
- Shift: 23:45-07:15 PST (night wing). This doc is the handoff to the 07:15 team. Quick TL;DR: short-lived latency spike in hosted-api (eu-west region) starting ~00:18; cascade of 504s and increased queueing for the text-generation route. Root cause early signal: autoscaler produced many small pods with incompatible quantized kernel selection which led to increased KV cache misses and transient OOMs on 80% of new replica starts.

Incident timeline (concise):
- 00:18 — Alert: Hosted-API route text-gen p95 latency from 120ms -> 2.1s; error-rate (504) rose from 0.1% -> 3.7% (INC-2027-01-05-1). Pager triggers: two on-call pages.
- 00:20 — SRE oncall (Maya) and infra (Carlos) join bridge; initial mitigation: scale down new replica group to 0 to stop churn.
- 00:26 — Observed pattern: new replicas repeatedly crash with OOM during model load; crash logs point at kernel-selection shim choosing quantized kernels that are not compatible with current runtime flags.
- 00:31 — Temporary mitigation: pin serving-runtime flag fallback-to-fp16=true and restart autoscaler. This reduced new-replica churn and errors began to fall.
- 00:40 — Traffic normalized; we kept the pinned flag until 03:00 while longer-term investigation progressed.
- 03:15 — Root cause hypothesis validated: a commit to kernel-selection heuristics (PR infra#512) introduced a condition where sequence-length heuristics favored quantized kernels without checking runtime-compatibility for the variant; combined with an autoscaler policy that aggressively spun up small pods for burst traffic, we got many pods trying to load the quantized variant concurrently causing KV cache pressure then OOM.

Actions taken (what we did):
- Immediate: scaled down autoscaler group, set fallback-to-fp16 flag, restarted control-plane router to re-evaluate variant routing.
- Post-incident: reverted heuristic change in a canary branch (PR 512 reverted) and opened a targeted rollback on staging.
- Communication: notified Customer Success for impacted customers (small set, EU region). Posted timely updates on #sre-oncall and #platform-status.

Runbook notes / updates (what to change in runbooks):
- Add a new quick-check section under "model-variant-load-failures": how to force fallback-to-fp16 and steps to gracefully drain replicas. Include exact CLI flags and k8s rollout commands.
- Add a troubleshooting flow for "rapid replica churn + OOM during model load": check kernel-selection version, autoscaler burst settings, pod start logs for "kv cache" and "kernel not compatible".
- Update autoscaler playbook to include a safety cap on concurrent replica startups for model-load-heavy routes (suggestion: cap concurrent startup to 4 per node pool for text-gen routes).
- Add a note to the canary checklist: verify kernel-selection matrix against runtime flags before rolling heuristics to prod.

Open follow-ups (owner / target date / status):
- SRE-1423: Formal postmortem draft and severity classification. Owner: Aisha Patel. Target: 2027-01-09. Status: in_progress.
- Infra-rollback: finalize and merge rollback of PR 512, then run canary in staging. Owner: Carlos Mendez. Target: 2027-01-07. Status: in_progress.
- Autoscaler policy change: implement concurrent-start cap and safety backoff. Owner: Oliver Grant. Target: 2027-01-12. Status: todo.
- Runbook patch: add quick-checks and exact CLI commands. Owner: Maya Chen. Target: 2027-01-08. Status: todo.
- Customer outreach: CS to run list of impacted customers and send tailored note. Owner: Priya Rao (CS). Target: 2027-01-06. Status: in_progress.

Metrics snapshot (when alert peaked):
- p95 latency (text-gen eu-west): 2.1s (baseline 120ms)
- error-rate 504: 3.7% (baseline 0.1%)
- CPU usage on new pods: spike to 95% during load (then crash)
- KV cache occupancy: +250% measured on control-plane metric (indicative of cache mismanagement)

Escalations / comms:
- Eng leads notified: @HeadOfInfra and @HeadOfSRE via Slack DM 00:35.
- Exec status: sent short note to ops@redwood about potential customer impact at 01:00 (kept high-level).
- Post-incident channel: #incident-review (created with notes and links).

Notes for next shift (what to watch for):
- Keep an eye on autoscaler startup rate in eu-west for text-gen routes. If new replicas > 6 in 5m window, escalate.
- Watch kernel-selection molecule: metric kernel-selection-version and fallback flags. If mismatch flagged, throw automated warning.
- Monitor KV-cache occupancy and eviction rate; if eviction spikes > 150% over baseline, consider immediate pin to fp16.

Temporary playbook snippets (copy/paste ready):
- Force fallback to FP16: 
  curl -X POST https://control-plane.api/redwood/config -d '{"serving_runtime": {"fallback_to_fp16": true}}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
- Drain new replicas: 
  kubectl scale deployment text-gen-eu-west --replicas=2 --namespace=redwood-hosted
  kubectl rollout restart deployment/router-eu-west -n redwood-hosted

Why this felt tricky / lessons learned (bullet observations):
- The combination of a subtle kernel-selection heuristic change + aggressive startup policy produced a non-linear failure mode. Individually both seemed low-risk.
- Our canary safety windows were insufficient for kernel-selection heuristics because the compatibility matrix is runtime-dependent (hardware + runtime flags).
- Observability: logs showed helpful OOM stack traces but we lacked a dedicated metric that correlates "pod-start kernel-selection mismatch" to customer errors — add one.

Attachments / pointers:
- Bridge logs and timestamps: link in linked_artifacts (INC-2027-01-05-1).
- Debug snippets saved to s3 (s3://redwood-debug/2027-01-05-kernel-ooms) — ping me if you need access.

Immediate risks remaining at handoff:
- If autoscaler policy rolls back to previous aggressive behavior before infra PR is fully reconciled, we could re-hit churn. Ensure feature gates are consistent across zones.
- PR reverts must be staged to not impact other regions; careful with config propagation.

Handoff checklist (for incoming shift):
- Confirm autoscaler concurrency cap is set in eu-west (check infra dashboard).
- Verify fallback-to-fp16 flag currently set to true; if not, set and monitor for 10m with no errors.
- Validate PR 512 rollback progress in staging and confirm canary results (link in linked_artifacts).
- Confirm customer outreach status with Priya.

Sign-off / notes:
- Night team: Maya Chen (oncall), Carlos Mendez (infra), Aisha Patel (postmortem lead) — we stabilized and kept customer impact limited. Leaving a number of follow-ups that should be resolved before next major rollout of kernel-selection heuristics.
- Incoming: please ping me directly in Slack @mchen if you need context or the raw debug bundle.

Quick raw notes / fragments (scratchpad preserved):
- saw logs: "kernel shim: selected quantized_x86_v3 but runtime flag unsupported -> memmap fallback failed"
- customer: acme-ads reported 5% request failures between 00:20-00:45 — confirmed in CS queue
- manual metric: rolling restart of router cleared downstream queueing within 12m

-- end of handoff --
